_meta.description: Deep-dive evaluation of 5 high-impact creative off-grid/hybrid demand applications for 1–20 MW microreactors with power requirements, incumbent displacement economics, and primary source citations.

applications.name: Spaceport Cryogenic Propellant Liquefaction & Pad Microgrids

power_profile.duty_cycle: Continuous 24/7 baseload with multi-megawatt pulse chilling prior to launch windows

incumbent.source: Long radial utility transmission feeders + long-haul diesel tanker trucking for liquid propellants
incumbent.costs_displaced: $150–$350/MWh delivered power + heavy boil-off product losses during transit and uninsulated storage

applications.microreactor_fit: Dedicated behind-the-meter microreactor powers continuous on-site electric chillers for liquid oxygen (LOX, -183°C), liquid methane (LCH4, -162°C), and liquid hydrogen (LH2, -253°C). Eliminates thousands of hazardous highway tanker deliveries and protects launch cadence from utility grid outages.

sources.label: The Space Review — Energy economics of orbital propellant production
sources.quote: liquefying a full load of methane... projected at around 55.2 megawatts

sources.label: NASA Technical Reports Server — Cryogenic Propellant Storage and Transfer
sources.quote: zero boil-off storage requires continuous active refrigeration

applications.name: Arctic Surveillance Radar & NORAD Modernization Outposts

power_profile.duty_cycle: 100% continuous flat baseload with 99.999% availability requirement

incumbent.source: Islanded diesel generator banks burning Arctic-grade diesel (DF-A)
incumbent.costs_displaced: $350–$850/MWh levelized cost due to fly-in and seasonal sea-lift/ice-road fuel delivery logistics

applications.microreactor_fit: 47+ radar stations across Alaska, Northern Canada, and Greenland (North Warning System modernization) require multi-year continuous power. Microreactors provide 3–10 year refueling cycles, black-start islanding capability, and eliminate vulnerable seasonal fuel resupply chains while complying with 10 U.S.C. 2920 resilience mandates.

sources.label: UCanPower — Arctic Microreactors for Defense Radar Infrastructure
sources.quote: evaluating deploying microreactors to two or more Alaska-based long-range radar sites by 2029

sources.label: Sandia National Laboratories — Arctic Microgrid Reliability
sources.quote: diesel fuel delivered to remote Arctic sites exceeds $15 per gallon in delivered cost

applications.name: Direct Air Capture (DAC) & Mineral Carbonation Hubs

power_profile.thermal_mwth: 10–100 MWth (80°C–120°C low-temperature steam for solid-sorbent desorption)

incumbent.source: Natural gas combined heat and power boilers or grid electricity + fossil fuel steam
incumbent.costs_displaced: Fossil combustion emissions reduce net capture efficiency by 20–35% unless zero-carbon heat is used

applications.microreactor_fit: Solid-sorbent DAC processes require 1.0–1.5 MWth of low-temperature heat (80–120°C) per thousand tonnes CO2 captured. Microreactors co-located at geological sequestration sites achieve 75–85% total thermal efficiency by utilizing turbine exhaust heat for desorption, yielding true net-negative carbon removal without transmission interconnection delays.

sources.label: MDPI Processes — Integration of Small Modular and Microreactors with Direct Air Capture
sources.quote: thermal output utilization increases from ~32% stand-alone to 76–85% in combined nuclear-DAC systems

sources.label: World Resources Institute — Direct Air Capture Energy and Resource Requirements
sources.quote: capturing 1 million tonnes of CO2 per year requires 100 to 300 MW of zero-carbon power

applications.name: Subsea Power Hubs & Deepwater Processing Modules

incumbent.source: Floating production gas turbines (FPSO) and high-voltage AC/DC seabed umbilical cables from shore
incumbent.costs_displaced: $50M–$200M per umbilical installation plus heavy turbine maintenance offshore

applications.microreactor_fit: Autonomous submerged microreactor modules provide localized 2–10 MWe power for seafloor multiphase pumps, gas compression stations, and submerged edge compute pods, operating maintenance-free for 5–10 years and eliminating long-distance high-voltage umbilical failures.

sources.label: Offshore Technology — Subsea Power Distribution and Submerged Nuclear Modules
sources.quote: subsea processing requires continuous megawatt-scale power independent of surface weather

applications.name: Biorefineries & Grain Processing Steam Cogeneration

incumbent.source: Natural gas fire-tube boilers and radial utility distribution feeders
incumbent.costs_displaced: $8–$14/MMBtu delivered natural gas + regional gas pipeline curtailment during winter freeze events

applications.microreactor_fit: Corn ethanol, biodiesel, and large-scale grain mills require massive continuous low-pressure process steam alongside heavy electric grinding loads. A 10–20 MWe microreactor configured for back-pressure steam extraction supplies 100% of facility electric and thermal load behind-the-meter, insulating operations from fossil price swings and pipeline interruptions.

sources.label: DOE Better Buildings — Combined Heat and Power in Food and Grain Processing
sources.quote: grain processing facilities operate with thermal-to-electric ratios between 2:1 and 4:1
